alignment.note: The Greek imperative Ἀκούετε ('Listen!') carries a paragraph marker (¶) and full stop, while the Vulgate separates Audite from the following clause with an explicit colon. Syriac ܫܡܥܘ stands without punctuation; the divergence is purely editorial and does not affect the reading.

Greek uses an articular present participle (ὁ σπείρων, 'the one sowing'), substantivising the agent with the definite article; the Vulgate renders this with a bare participle (seminans) and Syriac with the agent noun ܙܪܘܥܐ ('the sower'). All three denote the same figure but employ distinct nominal strategies.

Greek expresses purpose with the articular genitive infinitive τοῦ σπεῖραι, the Vulgate with the gerundive ad seminandum, and Syriac with the prefixed infinitive ܠܡܙܪܥ (lamed + infinitive). Each is the idiomatic purpose construction of its language, semantically equivalent ('to sow').
